bio.short: I'm Tobias Treppmann, a design leader in Berlin working closer to the model than to the screen. Fifteen-plus years across four Head- and Director-of-design tenures, most recently at Bibel TV — where an AI fundraising ecosystem I built solo runs on a Claude Project with follow-up-question loops and a Claude Skill that carries the same voice into in-app notifications, web banners, and video scripts. bio.long:
I'm Tobias Treppmann, a design leader based in Berlin, and lately my work sits closer to the model than to the screen. At Bibel TV I built a fundraising ecosystem end to end — analyzed which letters historically outperform, encoded the analysis into a Claude Project that asks follow-up questions before it drafts anything, built a web prototype for the generation flow, and shipped a Claude Skill that produces the follow-up notifications, web banners, and video scripts from the same source. All of it solo, at the layer where prompt design and product design stop being separable. I also designed, scoped, and shipped a Copilot skill for the customer-support team, introduced through a self-testing week and 1:1 sessions with each team member; adoption held across the team, including the most skeptical members, including the initially most skeptical person on the team.

Before Bibel TV I spent a year at ChurchDesk mapping a funeral-coordination process that ran on phone calls between funeral homes, parishes, and cemeteries. I reframed it from a booking feature into a booking capability wired deep into the platform. Days of phone-tag became hours; the acceptance rate landed at ninety percent; twenty-plus cemeteries came on board. At Ninox I co-defined the prompt-to-database onboarding with the CEO and technical co-founder in a stealth pre-product-team phase — prompt to database schema, rendered into the real data-model editor with direct manipulation and chat side by side, so a non-technical SME owner can own the schema within minutes of seeing it. In parallel I ran the design system as a structured cross-functional group: one design lead assigned, one engineer assigned, regular meeting rhythm, documented process for identifying component changes and escalating them.

What runs underneath all of that is a personal practice with the same tools this role customizes for Lovehoney. Claude Skills, Claude Projects, Claude Code, Claude Co-work, Microsoft Copilot, and a twelve-agent MCP-configured stack I self-host and use every day. I've been running the "Designing with and for AI" workshop series for designers and engineers since 2024 — and at Hypoport Hub SE I ran design-thinking training programs for executive leadership plus service teams that included HR, marketing, and other non-designer, non-engineer functions. I'm plain-spoken, comfortable in sensitive-context work (ChurchDesk was GDPR-plus across six countries), and Berlin is home.

context.company: Lovehoney Group — UK-owned adult retail group, 800+ employees across 11 offices, Bain-Capital-backed. Berlin office. Category is adult-wellness / sexual-wellbeing e-commerce.
context.role: AI Innovation and Enablement Specialist — an internal-tooling operator role, IC-shaped despite Specialist title. Owns the Claude Enterprise rollout function by function across the group, runs a Champions Programme of internal AI advocates, customizes Claude Skills / Claude Projects / Claude Code / MCP servers, facilitates workshops for both technical and non-technical audiences, and maps process inefficiencies into automations.
